title: A move in T1 costs time proportional to the length of the play: positionNames rebuilds the spoken text of every position on every move
location: site/src/components/tools/T01GameBoard.svelte:429 (const positionNames = $derived.by over k = 0..game.moves.length), read by site/src/components/board/History.svelte:44; the same derivation in T16Sandbox.svelte:391, T09Kostant.svelte:371, T05NumbersGameLab.svelte:213, T07SymbolicGame.svelte:362, T08WeylExplorer.svelte:376, T03FormFinder.svelte:285, T06Kaleidoscope.svelte:145, board/BoardSeed.svelte:62 (T15AffinePlayground.svelte:263 computes only the cursor's name above 50 positions)
claim: Every state change of T1 recomputes the strings 'After move k: ...' for all L+1 positions of the play (shownAt, inLabelOrder, spokenValue per position), although History shows only positionNames[cursor] above 50 positions, so the handler of one move grows linearly with L and becomes a long task on long plays the tool itself produces.
expected: SPEC 7.4 'Single source of truth': '... extends it by one position per move, so a move costs one engine call however long the play is'; lens attack 25: a handler time that does not grow with the length of the play; SPEC 7.6 'Main-thread work': no long task (50 ms) for a move.
observed: 12-cycle with chord 1-7 (Big), legal play from all ones, 1x on this container (4 processors, Node 22.22.0, Chromium 141): one Step press after 12 moves median 4.5 ms and 4.2 ms (two runs of seven presses); after Play to the end (20000 moves, the cap of 5.6) median 70.4 ms and 72.4 ms, every press a long task of 54 to 106 ms. After a 1999-move link (under the E-9 2000 boundary) on the same board in free play: click processing (Event Timing) median 12.0 ms against 2.2 ms after 10 moves at 1x, 36.6 against 8.9 ms at 4x with long tasks of 57 to 74 ms in 3 of 7 clicks. CPU profile of one click at 1999 moves: positionNames 6.5 ms of a 10.7 ms flush, appendWord under 1 ms. Play to the end itself, after the worker answers: one main-thread long task of 82 to 95 ms on the triangle and 112 to 150 ms on the 12-node board, of which positionNames 34 ms and the replay of the word (appendWord) 13 ms on the triangle.

refute.evidence:
Read at the gate commit 69546f0 with git show. The worktree was detached at the gate commit. npm ci was not run, because refute mode runs nothing from the build. The tree is clean and nothing was committed.

What the code does:
- site/src/components/tools/T01GameBoard.svelte:429-439 has `const positionNames = $derived.by(...)` with `for (let k = 0; k <= game.moves.length; k++) { const s = game.shownAt(k); ... inLabelOrder(game.board, v).map(spokenValue).join(', ') }`. It is passed to History at line 573.
- site/src/components/board/History.svelte reads `aria-valuetext={positionNames[cursor]}` when there are more than 50 positions. Up to 50 positions it reads `aria-label={positionNames[k]}` for each strip button.
- t01/model.ts:195-197: `inLabelOrder` calls the engine export `toPositions(board, labelOrder(board))` once per call. `toPositions` is imported from '@two-games/engine' at model.ts:8-22.
- t01/model.ts:448-457: `shownAt` maps every entry through the engine's `arith.show`.
- So each state change calls engine exports O(L) times (L+1 calls to toPositions, n(L+1) calls to show), besides the single position step that `appendWord` adds (model.ts:500-515, `after` = mutate or fire, plus toNumbers or toPopulation).
- So the per-move cost grows with L even when counted in engine calls, the narrow reading of 7.4.

Specification text:
- 7.4: no 'may', no 'unless', no qualifier.
- 4.0 [D] 'History': 'A visible strip of past positions can be scrubbed ... A strip of more than 50 positions is shown as a slider with a counter.' It requires no name for every position.
- 4.0 'One state, derived views' and 'Step and play to the end' ('Afterwards the history holds every position of the play') let the tool keep every position. They do not let it rebuild every position's text on each move.
- CONTRACTS.md:365 describes History.svelte only as 'the strip of past positions (slider above 50)'. It has no positionNames contract.

Phases:
- T1 and T9 are phase 1. T3, T15 and T16 are phase 2. T5 to T8 are phase 3. BoardSeed is phase 0.
- All are within gate G3. The lens scope table puts attack 25 in phases 1 to 7.

Records:
- No DECISIONS.md entry or decisions/*.md fragment at the gate commit records the full-play derivation.
- grep for positionNames, 'one engine call', 'per move', 7.4, 'long task', 'strip of' and aria-valuetext found no such record.
- decisions/P1-A5.md ('history, the state, view and mode choosers'; 'step, play to the end, the worker') is silent on it.
- The accepted LONG_LIST_REPLAY = 'sync' reading (DECISIONS.md, P1-A2 urlCodec entry) covers the one-time replay of a link on load, not the cost of each move.
- decisions/P2-A4.md records the opposite choice for T15: 'the strip is a slider with a counter above 50 positions (History.svelte), whose position names are computed only for the cursor'.

Earlier reports:
- reports/gate-G3.md at the gate commit has no open item on this.
- gate-G1.md's lead 'RT-04 the long-move-list replay on the main thread under the sync reading' is a different cause (link replay on load).
- No merge-P*-redteam-round*.md exists on disk; this is the first round.

The oracle is not involved: there is no mathematical value in dispute.

refute.evidence:
Read at gate commit 69546f023085e0573fff129b35dac7caebc6eca8: SPEC.md 5.6 in full, 5.1 (E-9, E-11), 5.5, 7.6, 4.0, T4 and T16 (SPEC 4), CONTRACTS.md 2.1, 2.4 and 4, DECISIONS.md, the decisions fragments P2-A3, P2-A5, P2-A7, MERGE, GATE and P3-A7, reports/gate-G2.md and gate-G3.md, and lens RT-07 (attack 24 and section 6).

(1) The 5.6 sentence has no qualifier ('may', 'unless'), and no other sentence allows several classify computations on one load. E-11: 'The test for finite type is `classify`, whose verdict is kept in a `WeakMap` from board objects to verdicts inside the engine module'. The cache is keyed by object, so it does not remove repeated computations on freshly built objects.

(2) The records read 'once' as a count per load:
- DECISIONS.md / decisions/P2-A7.md, 'P2-A7: the verdict cache in state.ts': 'resolveBoard(spec) ... calls classify once ... Reason: SPEC 5.6 last sentence'.
- decisions/P2-A5.md, 'P2-A5: the verdict, the T4 items left out, D19': '`buildVerdict` on one board object per board load (one classify call, cached)'.
- Plan P2-A7, section 1: 'every tool decides whether its board is of finite type from one call of `classify`, made by `resolveBoard` when the board is loaded'. The plan allows a second classify only in the worker ('that second `classify` happens in another thread and is allowed').
- T04ClassificationLab.svelte line 10, at the gate commit: 'One board object per edit state (`theBoard`), passed to every engine call, so that classify runs once per board (5.6, E-11)'.
- Yet state.ts resolveBoard runs `buildBoard(spec); verdictOf(board)` on every call, and T04 calls resolveBoard at :78 (theBoard), :119 (loadLink validation) and in labelsStartAtZero, besides urlCodec.ts:195 and BoardEditor.svelte:71. The build itself does not keep the rule its records state.

(3) Phase: T4 (phase 2) and T16 (phase 2) are SPEC 4 headings; classify and smallestNonfiniteSubboard are phase 2 in the 5.3 rows. The gate covers phases 0 to 3.

(4) The oracle does not apply: the finding concerns call counts and timing, not values.

(5) 7.6 carries [D], but the build's behaviour is not a choice within its text. 5.6, E-9 and E-11 carry no [D]. No D1 to D19 default covers this. The owner's entry 'OWNER: gate G3's lab item accepted as machine-bound' accepts only 'Total Blocking Time 242 to 332 ms on M0 to M5'. It does not cover tool routes, the main-thread rule or the classify count.

(6) Earlier reports:
- gate-G2.md line 124 lists only 'the T4 counter's main-thread search on the star' as a lead, which is a different cause.
- gate-G3.md has no item on classify per load, and its line 5 names gate commit 76b502f, not 69546f0 (the harness's gate is the owner commit above it).

refute.reason:
not refuted: the cause (resolveBoard builds and classifies a new board object on every call, so one load computes classify 4 to 5 times) contradicts the unqualified 5.6 sentence, which the builders' own records read as one call per load.
- R1 fails: no 'may' or qualifier, and E-11's per-object cache presumes the object is reused.
- R2 fails for the cause, though partly holds against the 7.6 half. 7.6 says 'No engine call ... may become a long task (50 ms) on that phone', which is a per-call rule on the owner's phone. The finding adds several calls together on this container, which MERGE records as about 2.3 times slower than the reference processor. Since the cause stands, this partial misreading does not refute the finding (RT-VERIFY 5.5).
- R3 fails: T4, T16, classify and smallestNonfiniteSubboard are all phase 2, inside the gate.
- R4 does not apply: no value is in dispute.
- R5 fails: 5.6 and E-11 are unlabelled, and no section 10 default or owner entry covers repeated classify or tool-route load time. The G3 lab acceptance covers only lesson TBT.
- R6 fails: no record in gate-G2.md or gate-G3.md, and no earlier round.
Severity: the RED-TEAM-COMMON 4 rubric puts 'a behaviour the specification states is missing or wrong' at major. Lens attack 24 would grade the bare count minor unless the repeated calls together form a long task, which the 7.6 reading above leaves open, so the claimed major stands on the rubric.

title: The index page (one Game Board) fetches the whole engine, 12037 B gzip, while its island needs 4306 B

refute.evidence: Read at gate commit 69546f0 with git show; refute mode, so nothing was built or run, npm ci was skipped and the worktree is clean. SPEC 7.6 (heading [D]): "Islands share code: the Svelte runtime, the core of the engine and the board components are fetched once per page". The shared code it lists does not include a tool registry. The table's tool row is "the tool's own code with the engine functions only it uses" and its lesson row is "the first tool of the page, and any other tool in view". There is no "may" and no qualifying clause. RT-07 section 6 excludes only "the sub-figures ... (shared code 45 kB, a tool's own code 30 kB) when the route's limit holds". This finding is about which modules a route ships, not about the 30 kB figure. Attacks 12 and 35 of the same lens treat unused code in a tool chunk within its limit as minor. Build: site/src/tools/index.ts:31 has import.meta.glob('./registry/T*.ts', { eager: true }); urlCodec.ts:20 imports boardsOffered from '../tools/index'; all 11 tool components import decodeState from urlCodec. registry/T02.ts imports t02/presets.ts, which at top level calls roots on A3 and A2, positiveRoots on A3, and orbitGraph on the triangle with CAPS.layersOffFinite. t08/presets.ts:44-52 runs weylOrder, legalLayers, countCompleteGames and commutationClassSize on A3 at module load. Its own comment says this keeps "the registry ... cheap on every page", so the builders knew the registry loads on every page. CONTRACTS 5.2 (plan) puts presets and boards in registry entries "collected with import.meta.glob". It does not require eager loading in the client or engine work at module load. CONTRACTS 4 makes decodeState(search, tool, defaults) synchronous, which needs the offered boards by tool id but not every tool's presets. DECISIONS.md records these facts only as builder notes: P1-A2 "rule 8 for an unregistered tool" (boardsOffered from the registry), P1-A6 "Captions take their numbers from the engine at module load", P2-A2 and P2-A3 "the registry module, which is loaded on every tool page". None of them is a [D] text, a section 10 default or an owner's answer. The OWNER entry of 2026-10-17 accepts only the G3 TBT numbers as machine-bound, not what the chunks hold. On R6: no merge-P3-redteam-round*.md exists in /home/user/mutation_game/reports/. gate-G3.md section 12 lists the first tool's hydration task only as a lead, which is not a tracked record of this cause. Partial errors that leave the cause standing: (a) the quote "which only the tool can shorten" comes from DECISIONS.md "MERGE: P3 stage 3.3", not from gate-G3.md section 8, which reads "what remains over the line is the hydration task of the first tool". (b) The specRef "Main-thread work" rule ("No engine call on the main thread may become a long task (50 ms)") is not broken by the finding's own figures: t02/presets.ts takes 31 to 46 ms inclusive at four times slowdown, and that time spans several engine calls. gate-G3.md names 76b502f as its gate commit; the report is in the tree at 69546f0, the commit above it.
refute.reason: not refuted: none of the six refutations holds. R1 fails because 7.6 has no permitting clause and the lens excludes only the 45 and 30 kB figures. R2 fails because the finding reads the tool and lesson rows correctly; only the source of one quote and the long-task part of its specRef are wrong, and the cause stands without them. R3 fails because every tool involved belongs to phases 1 to 3 and size limits apply from G1. R4 does not apply because the claim is not mathematical. R5 fails because the eager registry and the captions computed at load lie outside 7.6's [D] text, are recorded only as builder notes, and the owner's 17 October answer covers the TBT number only. R6 fails because no earlier round or open item records this cause. Severity stays minor: no limit is exceeded and no single engine call is shown above 50 ms, and RT-07's own level for unused code in a chunk within its limit is minor, a case RED-TEAM-COMMON 4 does not name.
